questions.stem: What elements are carbohydrates made of?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates contain only three elements: carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen, in the general ratio Cn(H2O)n.

questions.stem: What is the molecular formula of glucose?
questions.explanation: Glucose has the molecular formula C6H12O6. It is a monosaccharide (simple sugar) and is the most common sugar used in respiration.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disaccharide?
questions.explanation: Maltose is a disaccharide formed when two glucose molecules join together by a condensation reaction. Glucose and fructose are monosaccharides, and starch is a polysaccharide.

questions.stem: What type of bond joins two monosaccharides together?
questions.explanation: Two monosaccharides are joined by a glycosidic bond, formed during a condensation reaction that releases a molecule of water.

questions.stem: Sucrose is made from which two monosaccharides?
questions.explanation: Sucrose (table sugar) is a disaccharide formed from one glucose molecule and one fructose molecule joined by a glycosidic bond.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of glucose in living organisms?

options.text: To act as an energy source for respiration

questions.explanation: Glucose is the primary energy source for cells. It is broken down during respiration to release energy in the form of ATP.

questions.stem: What is the difference between alpha and beta glucose?

options.text: The OH group on carbon-1 is in a different position
They have different numbers of carbon atoms

questions.explanation: Alpha and beta glucose have the same molecular formula (C6H12O6) but differ in the position of the hydroxyl (-OH) group on carbon-1. This structural difference affects the polymers they form.
